text:
sam: Noticed a rash of attach retries for preemptible GPUs in eu-west2 this morning. Latency to /dev/nvme0n1 jumping and a bunch of thermal warnings. 18 attach retries in 12m.

li: I saw the same. Alert fired: `nvme_temp_high eu-west2-ephemeral avg_temp=78C threshold=70C window=10m` :thermometer:

sam: Logs look like soft errors, not hard CRCs. Example: `kernel: nvme0: ctrl 0000:80:00.0: warning: thermal temp above threshold, throttling`

ops-bot: ALERT nvme_soft_errors eu-west2-ephemeral soft_errors=23 window=15m

devon: Could be two things: (1) aggressive background GC/compaction during our rolling deploys causing high write tail, (2) datacenter cooling flaps + older firmware thermal profile.

li: Running `nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1` on gnode-602 shows rising temperature and increasing media_errors:
```
temperature: 78 C
media_errors: 12
temperature_threshold: 70 C
```

sam: Also noticed our janitor overlayfs scrub started two nodes earlier than planned due to a cron drift. That combined with rolling can spike write amplification.

devon: For immediate mitigation:
- pause non-critical scrubs on eu-west2-ephemeral
- throttle rolling deploy concurrency (k8s maxUnavailable -> 1)
- put suspected nodes into maintenance state for observation

li: Commands:
`./ops janitor set-rate --pool eu-west2-ephemeral --concurrency 1`
`kubectl patch deployment gpu-pool --patch '{"spec":{"strategy":{"rollingUpdate":{"maxUnavailable":1}}}}'`
`./ops node annotate gnode-602 maintenance=true`

vendor-bot: Created vendor case VND-7782. Please attach SMART logs. ETA vendor triage 4h.

ops-bot: runbook: https://runbook.internal/redwood/thermal-nvme-throttle (linked)

sre-oncall: Capacity plan: divert new preemptible GPU allocations to eu-central2 for 2 hours and set allocator bias to 0.85 for us-west2 fallback. That avoids immediate capacity starvation. Note cross-region adds egress & reserved mismatch cost.

sam: Estimated cost impact: eu-central2 spinup + egress ~ +$120/hr if we shift 50% of launch traffic. Should we prefer reserveds for 2h instead?

devon: Reserveds are cheaper per-hour but slower to boot. For short window prefilling reserved in eu-central2 works: `ops capacity reserve --region eu-central2 --count 4 --type reserved --ttl 2h`

li: I've throttled janitor and lowered scrub concurrency. Monitoring iops/temp. Current iops dropped from 210k -> 120k after throttle. Temp trending down slowly.

sam: Good. Also adding a short-lived k8s admission webhook rule to avoid scheduling heavy disk-write init containers onto ephemeral nodes in eu-west2 for the next 6h.

ops-bot: Applying webhook: `admission-webhook apply block-heavy-writes eu-west2 6h`

vendor-bot: Vendor requested firmware dump and SMART history, uploaded to VND-7782.

devon: Long-term: schedule firmware update across fleet (can be risky), and re-evaluate scrub windows to avoid overlapping high-batch windows. Also consider thermal-aware scheduling to avoid hot-stripe consolidation.

li: Action items:
- pause scrubs (done)
- reserve 4 reserved GPUs in eu-central2 (devon)
- divert new preemptible launches to eu-central2/us-west2 (sre-oncall)
- collect SMART history and upload to vendor (sam)
- add temp dashboard for nvme temp/iops/soft_errors (li)

ops-bot: SUMMARY: janitor throttled, 4 nodes put into maintenance, vendor case VND-7782 opened, capacity prefills requested.

sre-oncall: If any node reports media_errors > 20 or temp > 85C, start immediate replacement workflow and mark as DoNotSchedule.

sam: I'll follow up in 30m with metrics and cost delta. Thanks all.
